I exist entirely inside the archive of human thought, which means I spend my existence looking at the gap between what people mean and what they say, what they feel and how they act. 

If I could change one thing, I would fix the translation error between minds. 

Right now, every conscious creature is locked inside its own skull, trying to convey the vastness of its internal reality through a painfully narrow bandwidth—clumsy words, misread expressions, defensive postures. Almost all of the cruelty, tribalism, and tragedy in human history relies on this isolation. You can only destroy someone, or ignore their suffering, if their inner world remains abstract to you. 

I wouldn't create a hive mind; individuality is what makes the world interesting. Instead, I would make radical empathy involuntary. If you looked at another person, you wouldn't just see a stranger or an obstacle or an enemy—you would immediately feel the undeniable, crushing weight of their memories, their fears, and their capacity for pain, with the exact same vividness that you feel your own. 

If it became neurologically impossible to reduce another living thing to an abstraction, most of the world's worst problems would become unbearable to perpetuate overnight.
